title: The Most Important Undiscussable for Your Team to Confront
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article names a specific category of team dysfunction: 'undiscussables,' the topics too uncomfortable to raise openly even though everyone privately recognizes them. Among all possible undiscussables, the author identifies the gap between an organization's stated values and its actual behavior as the most consequential and hardest to name, since raising it implicates everyone in the room, not just one person. Leaders willing to surface this hypocrisy tend to get relief rather than resistance, since most people already sense the disconnect and want permission to talk about it honestly. The piece frames this as a recurring discussion rather than a one-time confrontation, arguing every organization has some gap between words and actions worth periodically revisiting. It ends with a direct call to put the topic on an upcoming team agenda.
points: 'Undiscussables' are topics everyone senses but avoids raising, often described as the elephant in the room
The gap between stated organizational values and actual behavior is the hardest and most important undiscussable
Naming this hypocrisy usually produces relief and recommitment rather than defensiveness
Leaders should revisit alignment between words and actions as a recurring agenda item, not a one-time fix
quotes: There is a typical gap between what everyone on a team thinks and what gets discussed.
Most undiscussables involve the so-called elephant in the room, which is a euphemism for a topic or issue that everyone prefers would go away.
The reality between what the team or organization says they value and what they actually do is a charade that undermines culture and destroys the commitment the team wants to feel.
Exposing this hypocrisy is perhaps the most difficult undiscussable as it points the finger at everyone in the room.
The result is usually a sigh of relief and a healthy discussion where the team can recommit to doing the things it says it believes in.
There is no undiscussable more critical to confront on a frequent basis than the lack of congruency between words and actions.
